video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about wrapping an old callback API so other code can simply await it: Completion Handler, Callback Bridging & Resume Once, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Completion Handler - A closure you pass to a function, which the function calls later when its work is done.
Callback Bridging - Wrapping an old callback API in an async function, so callers can simply use await.
Resume Once - The rule that a continuation must be resumed exactly one time, never zero times and never twice.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Completion Handler, Callback Bridging & Resume Once in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Completion Handler, Callback Bridging, Resume Once 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Completion Handler - A closure you pass to a function, which the function calls later when its work is done.
한국어: Completion Handler: 함수에 전달하는 클로저로, 작업이 끝나면 함수가 나중에 호출함

Callback Bridging - Wrapping an old callback API in an async function, so callers can simply use await.
한국어: Callback Bridging: 오래된 콜백 API를 async 함수로 감싸서 호출하는 쪽이 await를 쓰게 하는 것

Resume Once - The rule that a continuation must be resumed exactly one time, never zero times and never twice.
한국어: Resume Once: 컨티뉴에이션을 정확히 한 번만 재개해야 한다는 규칙으로, 0번도 두 번도 안 됨

landscape.hook: Can you explain Completion Handler, Callback Bridging and Resume Once in English?

dialogue.title: Wrap the old callback API

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the old SDK still takes a completion handler, and I want to use await.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A completion handler is a closure the function calls later when the work is done.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. How do I get rid of the nested closures?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do callback bridging. Wrap `old` in an async function with a continuation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote `modern`, and it works. But sometimes the app hangs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check the error path. Does every branch call `resume`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. When the SDK returns an error, I do nothing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the bug. The rule is resume once, never zero times.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And not twice either, I guess?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Resuming twice is a crash. So resume once on every path.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. I will bridge the completion handler and test both paths.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Callback bridging is simple when you resume once.
The old SDK takes a completion handler.
